key_insight: VLA-JEPA trains a latent world model that predicts future task-relevant states without leaking pixel-level cues, so the model learns action-relevant dynamics instead of appearance or nuisance motion.
problem_solved: Current VLA pretraining objectives get anchored to pixel variation and nuisance motion, causing appearance bias and information leakage that hurt downstream action-conditioned policies.
method: JEPA-style latent prediction: learn to predict future latent states (a compact world model) rather than raw pixels.
Leakage-free targets: design the target encoder and training pipeline so predicted latents cannot access appearance/nuisance signals from target frames.
Action-conditioned dynamics & alignment: condition latent predictions on action/context and align latent space with language and policy objectives for VLA tasks.
impact: Leads to more robust, generalizable vision-language-action representations that reduce appearance bias and improve performance of action-conditioned policies from internet-scale video pretraining.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: encoders -> latent bottleneck -> JEPA predictor with a 'no-leak' barrier shown between target pixels and target latents.
Before vs after comparison: bar or line charts showing reduced sensitivity to appearance change and improved downstream policy metrics.
Latent trajectory visualization: sequence of latent states illustrating action-conditioned transitions vs pixel-space motion.
Icon panel: small icons for ‘video data’, ‘language’, ‘actions’, and ‘robust policies’ to show modalities and outcomes.
paper_title: VLA-JEPA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Model with Latent World Model
paper_authors: Jingwen Sun, Wenyao Zhang, Zekun Qi, Shaojie Ren, Zezhi Liu
